entities.summary:
Phaedrus, son of Pythocles, of the Myrrhinus deme, was an ancient Athenian aristocrat associated with the inner-circle of the philosopher Socrates. Born into a prominent family, he was educated in the traditional Athenian arts and sciences. In 415 BC, Phaedrus was indicted for profaning the Eleusinian Mysteries during the Peloponnesian War, forcing him to flee Athens. This event led to a significant reevaluation of the role of aristocrats in Athenian society and the relationship between philosophy and politics. The consequences of Phaedrus' actions can still be felt in the modern-day understanding of the intersection of philosophy and politics.

He was a philosopher and thinker from Athens who was recognized for his contributions to Western philosophy (443 BCE, Athens–392 BCE). Recognized as a landmark figure with global significance (referenced in 0 Wikipedia editions). Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.
